profile.summary: Anusha Sirigiri studies entrepreneurship, strategy and strategic human capital: how start-ups are staffed and structured as they grow, and how entrepreneurs can make better decisions. Her start-up work uses employee-level data on Indian internet and consumer digital start-ups to ask when experienced hires and formal structure help a young firm scale, and she has co-written on turning the 'scientific approach' (treat your idea as a theory, test it, update) into practical tools. Earlier, as part of a large US study of 757 information workers, she co-authored papers using phones, wearables and social media to measure employee wellbeing and job performance.

themes.name: Scaling start-ups: structure and talent
themes.description: How hiring experienced (IT and non-IT) employees and adding hierarchy or functional teams relate to the growth of Indian internet start-ups, and how this changes as the firm matures.

themes.name: Entrepreneurial decision-making and wellbeing
themes.description: Practical tools and design principles for the scientific approach to entrepreneurial decisions, and work on effectuation and entrepreneurs' wellbeing.

themes.name: Sensing job performance and wellbeing
themes.description: Using phones, wearables, beacons and LinkedIn data to measure how daily activity and role clarity relate to workers' wellbeing and job performance.

themes.name: Methods for large sensing studies
themes.description: Practical lessons on running long multi-sensor studies: collecting social media data, filling in missing data, and predicting who will keep complying.
